PullRequest.Title: chore: bump foundry-local-sdk to 2.x
PullRequest.Body:
This PR removes several steps specific to the foundry-local-sdk package now that its post-installation process can be customized more with environment variables.

Verification product build: https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=472517&view=results
Verification CI build: https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=472516&view=results

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after cancellation wiring and the normal user `cancel()` call path are explicit. The exact model byte size is not in-repo, but the mechanism applies to any nontrivial uncached model and the configured model is a 0.6B ASR model.
Findings.PerformanceResource: model-download network bytes, filesystem writes, and downloader CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Waste grows with the bytes remaining in the uncached 0.6B model when the user cancels; an early cancellation can leave nearly the entire model transfer running.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: continued bandwidth and disk/CPU consumption after dictation cancellation
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The service created an `AbortController`, wired `_modelPrepareCts` cancellation to `ac.abort()`, and passed `ac.signal` to `model.download`, so `cancel()` or service disposal stopped the transfer.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added SDK 2.x call invokes `model.download` with only the progress callback, while `cancel()` still merely cancels `_modelPrepareCts`; that token is checked only after the download resolves and can no longer stop the active model transfer.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 563 replaces the prior `model.download(..., ac.signal)` invocation and removes the cancellation subscription, directly severing the only abort path for this network operation.
Findings.Title: Keep first-use model downloads cancellable
Findings.Impact: If a user cancels first-use dictation while the model is downloading, cancellation returns but the utility process continues fetching and writing the large model until completion or network failure.
Findings.Evidence: `cancel()` at line 781 calls `_modelPrepareCts?.cancel()`, and disposal does the same. The changed download await at line 563 has no signal or token; the next cancellation check is after it completes. The deleted hunk explicitly bridged this token to an AbortSignal passed into the same download call.
Findings.Recommendation: Restore an abortable SDK 2.x download path and wire `_modelPrepareCts` to it; if the new API offers no per-download signal, cancel by tearing down/recreating the downloader or utility worker and await that cleanup rather than leaving the transfer detached.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The glob semantics, five-target SDK layout documented and consumed by this diff, package-task arguments, and exact-target runtime gate are all explicit. Only the binary sizes—and therefore the magnitude, not the mechanism—are unknown.
Findings.PerformanceResource: native-addon bytes in every product archive, installer, and installed tree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The excess grows with the SDK's prebuild target count: the package contains two addons for each of five supported targets, while one product can load only one target pair.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: larger product/update downloads, more installation I/O, and additional disk usage for every desktop user
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous filter excluded the SDK's entire prebuild tree; after the SDK upgrade the product needs two addons for its own runtime target, but no foreign-platform copies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added `prebuilds/**/foundry_local_node.node` include uses an unrestricted target wildcard, and the adjacent preload include does the same, so `packageTask(platform, arch, ...)` retains both addons from every SDK prebuild directory instead of just the product's loadable target.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 263 newly re-includes `**/foundry-local-sdk/prebuilds/**/foundry_local_node.node`; the next added line identically includes every target's preload addon, whereas the deleted filter excluded all prebuilds.
Findings.Title: Package only the target platform's Foundry addons
Findings.Impact: Each packaged desktop build carries up to ten native addon binaries although its support gate can use only two. Every installation and update transfers and stores the other targets' binaries.
Findings.Evidence: `packageTask` has the concrete `platform` and `arch`, but calls `getFoundryLocalExcludeFilter()` without them. The new include at line 263 matches every directory under `foundry-local-sdk/prebuilds/**`; `SUPPORTED_TARGETS` lists five target pairs, and the renderer support check permits only the current `${platform}-${arch}` pair (with the existing macOS arm64 mapping nuance).
Findings.Recommendation: Parameterize the filter with the package platform/arch and re-include only the two addon files for the single runtime target that build can load (mapping the universal macOS build to darwin-arm64).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The diff explicitly documents and implements package-loaded addons plus a shared-library override, and the tarball/cold-cache path is direct. Only the addon sizes, hence the severity, are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: duplicate `.node` addon bytes downloaded, extracted, and retained in the per-user runtime cache
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every cold runtime cache downloads two duplicate addon binaries once per SDK runtime version; cost scales with their compressed/uncompressed sizes and version churn.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: extra first-dictation latency, network transfer, extraction work, and cache disk usage
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous product excluded its sole addon and the runtime tarball supplied the addon actually loaded from the cache, so that transfer was required.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The product now deliberately bundles both SDK addons and configures `libraryPath` only for shared libraries, but `requiredSdkNativeFileNames` newly forces both `.node` files into the CDN tarball and runtime validation requires them in the cache as well.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 132 newly lists both packaged addon names as required SDK files for the staging tree that is archived and uploaded by `buildOne`.
Findings.Title: Leave bundled addons out of the runtime tarball
Findings.Impact: On the first dictation after each runtime-version change, users must download and extract cached copies of both addons even though the SDK loads the packaged copies.
Findings.Evidence: The new gulp filter keeps `foundry_local_node.node` and `foundry_local_preload.node` in the product. `LocalTranscriptionService` then calls `configureNativeLoader({ libraryPath })` for the shared-library cache, while line 132 requires those same addons in `buildOne`'s tarball and `requiredRuntimeFileNames` requires them after download.
Findings.Recommendation: Build and validate the CDN payload from only the shared libraries used through `libraryPath`; omit the two `.node` files from staging and from runtime cache completeness checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaging and delivering a desktop VS Code build or update
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The packaging stream must collect dependencies and write the ASAR/product archive before publication; users then transfer and install that archive on every install/update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and archive native addon files from every SDK prebuild target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to ten addon files per product instead of the two for its runtime target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All Foundry prebuild files were excluded; the upgraded layout requires only the current target's two addons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds archive construction and install I/O; all included bytes also become part of the distribution artifact.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: product distribution/update service consuming packageTask output
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the packaged application/update containing retained dependency files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One product transfer per install/update, inflated by up to eight unusable addon binaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No SDK addon bytes were present in the product archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The download must complete before installation/update can finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of SDK prebuild targets (five documented targets) times two addon binaries, rather than the one loadable target times two addons.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Gulp filters one merged dependency stream; the extra files are serialized into each product archive. Distribution concurrency does not reduce per-user transferred bytes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node-modules restoration can avoid rebuilding dependencies in CI, but it does not remove the foreign-platform addon files from the resulting product archive; every produced version and user update carries them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unrestricted glob, five-target SDK layout, package arguments, and exact-target runtime gate are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository evidence does not provide compressed addon sizes, so exact download and disk inflation is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: target-agnostic includes retain every platform's addons in each platform product.

Scenarios.Scenario: First on-device dictation with cold runtime and model caches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before a transcription session opens, the utility process downloads and extracts one target runtime tarball, imports/configures the SDK, queries the catalog, then downloads and loads the selected model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the per-target runtime tarball from the VS Code CDN.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold-cache request per runtime version after in-process coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary downloaded a tarball containing one addon that was actually loaded from cache plus shared libraries; the changed tarball now contains two addons already bundled in the product.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks SDK configuration and model preparation on first dictation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write, extract, verify, and promote the runtime payload into the user cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction and promotion per target/version on a cold cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing extraction handled the required cached addon/core payload; the diff adds two duplicate `.node` files to extracted and retained content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before SDK manager creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the 0.6B ASR model on catalog cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transfer per uncached model, coalesced by `_modelPromise`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transfer existed and accepted an AbortSignal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session creation waits for model download and load, while capture audio is buffered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the lazy utility worker and issue the start RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker/channel on first use and one start RPC per dictation session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lazy utility-process boundary existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the process hosting runtime/model work; unchanged cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target tarball per runtime version and one model per uncached selected model; the diff adds two packaged-addon copies to the tarball payload.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one utility process, runtime requests are coalesced by `inFlight` and model preparation by `_modelPromise`. Separate windows can still race runtime downloads, but atomic promotion handles that pre-existing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold runtime cache performs one CDN transfer; warm cache verifies a marker plus five files and skips network. Cold model cache performs one model transfer; warm model cache skips download.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: product packaging explicitly keeps both addons, runtime setup uses the cache as `libraryPath` for shared libraries, and tarball staging/validation explicitly includes both addons.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native addon sizes and CDN timings are not present; the duplicate-byte mechanism is certain but its latency contribution relative to shared libraries/model is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager transfer: both packaged addons are redundantly downloaded, extracted, and cached on first use.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel dictation while the first model download is running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The cancel RPC awaits session disposal and resets UI/session state; resource cleanup should abort the in-flight model network operation even though that operation is no longer on the user's post-cancel critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the user cancellation to the utility-process service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cancel RPC per canceled on-device session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cancel RPC canceled `_modelPrepareCts`, which was bridged to the download AbortSignal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC returns after local teardown, but no longer releases the active model network boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the selected Foundry model and write it to the cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached model transfer; after the diff it continues to completion/failure despite one cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cancellation invoked `AbortController.abort()` and the signal was passed to `model.download`; the diff removes that bridge and signal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It becomes detached from the completed cancel path but continues consuming bandwidth, disk I/O, and CPU.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Bytes remaining in the uncached model at cancellation time; an early cancel leaves nearly the full 0.6B-model artifact transfer outstanding.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one model preparation promise runs per service/model, but cancellation no longer terminates it; repeated same-model starts reuse the detached promise rather than adding more transfers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only cold model caches trigger the issue. A warm cache skips `model.download`; a partially/completely downloaded cache changes subsequent SDK behavior but does not bound the current detached transfer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: both the deleted abort wiring and current cancel/token call path are explicit, with the next token check only after download completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact artifact size and how often users cancel during first-use setup are unknown; remaining-transfer cost depends on cancel timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression: normal cancel/disposal no longer stops the expensive model transfer.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI dependency restore and dictation runtime publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On node-modules cache misses, NuGet authentication and npm install run; publish jobs then build a target runtime by staging SDK files, fetching missing ONNX packages, compressing one tarball, and uploading it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/azure-pipelines/* product build YAML npm install steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run SDK postinstall with authenticated NuGet feed access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK install per node-modules cache miss/job, replacing a separate post-install helper invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: npm install ran with the SDK lifecycle disabled, followed by the custom installer; the diff folds native installation into npm install rather than proving an added invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency installation blocks compilation as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download ONNX Runtime and ONNX Runtime GenAI NuGet packages when absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two sequential packages per produced target, with feed fallback only after failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior producer fetched three artifacts (Foundry Core plus two ONNX artifacts), also sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both required packages must be staged before tar compression/upload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload one target runtime tarball to the CDN on publish runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One upload per supported publish target/job; unsupported targets and non-publish builds skip it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-target publication boundary existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication waits for build and upload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy native files, extract NuGet archives, gzip the staging tree, hash it, and remove staging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One staging tree and tarball per supported publish target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same build shape staged one addon and a separate core directory; changed content does not establish additional collection cardinality beyond the duplicate-addon finding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One host dependency restore per cache miss; runtime publication handles one effective target per job and two NuGet artifacts after skip-if-present checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: NuGet artifacts are downloaded sequentially inside `fetchDependencyLibraries`; pipeline jobs for different platforms/architectures run independently. Node-modules cache-hit conditions skip installation work where configured.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node-modules cache hits skip npm install in node-module jobs. Runtime staging uses `skipIfPresent`, avoiding a NuGet package download when the expected library already exists in the SDK target directory; service-index lookups are cached per build invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary cardinality and cache conditions; low for any unmeasured SDK-internal install cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK 2.x postinstall implementation duration is outside the repository, so no install-time regression beyond explicit boundary counts can be established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable pipeline performance regression: expensive boundary counts are unchanged or reduced, aside from payload content already reported.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer sends PCM chunks over IPC to a lazy utility process; native session appends are serialized, inference streams results back, and stop drains queued appends and native output.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send audio chunks and session control between renderer and utility process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per audio chunk plus start/stop control calls, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Append ordering and stop drainage remain on transcription/finalization paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/use ONNX native libraries, append PCM, run inference, and stream results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized append per chunk and one result stream per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK/runtime version changes library implementation, but repository evidence does not prove changed inference multiplicity or a GPU execution path; the configured model is labeled CPU-only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines warm transcription throughput and finalization latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Audio duration and capture chunk count; append cardinality remains one native append per captured chunk.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single FIFO `_appendChain` preserves audio order; one active transcription session exists, and the stream consumer runs in the background.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With runtime and model cached, no download occurs; runtime performs bounded existence checks and the loaded model/model promise is reused in the utility process.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that call cardinality and scheduling are unchanged; insufficient evidence for a native inference regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The SDK 2.x native runtime's measured inference speed is not represented in the repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable warm-inference issue; the removed Linux GPU package was investigated but the product's model is explicitly presented as CPU-only and no GPU provider selection path was found.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 29 changed files. Submitted three findings: all-target addon fan-out into every product package, duplicate addon transfer in the first-use runtime tarball, and loss of cancellation for model downloads. Build boundary counts, cache/coalescing behavior, and warm transcription scheduling yielded no further supported regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
